findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket are not encrypted at rest by default.
No acl attribute or public access block is specified, leaving the bucket to inherit default provider/account behavior instead of an explicit private setting, increasing risk of unintended exposure.
The bucket stores ledger export data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, meaning sensitive financial data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so model artifacts are stored without encryption at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so operational runbook data is stored without encryption at rest.

The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid canned ACL (the intended value was likely 'log-delivery-write'); an invalid ACL can cause apply-time failure or unexpected access behavior on this sensitive bucket that aggregates logs from other buckets, risking unintended access grants.

force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be deleted without recourse, and combined with the absence of versioning, this creates risk of irrecoverable loss of archived reports data.

The object is uploaded without specifying a kms_key_id or server_side_encryption parameter, and the destination bucket itself lacks default encryption, so this potentially sensitive vendor roster file is stored in plaintext.
